title: Building Production-Ready Shiny Apps
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of building production-ready shiny apps and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply application architecture in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Building Production-Ready Shiny Apps is part of Interactive Application Development with Shiny. Start with application architecture and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: An interactive Shiny app connects validated inputs to reactive calculations and outputs; it also needs error states and data-protection boundaries.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: An interactive Shiny app connects validated inputs to reactive calculations and outputs; it also needs error states and data-protection boundaries. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.title: Application Architecture
items.text: Explain application architecture in the context of building production-ready shiny apps, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.title: User Feedback and Error Messages
items.text: For user feedback and error messages, include a failing or boundary case and explain how it should be detected without silently losing information.

items.title: Load and Performance Testing
items.text: Turn load and performance testing into a check with a clear condition, expected result and an example that should fail.

items.title: Accessibility and Usability
items.text: Explain accessibility and usability in the context of building production-ready shiny apps, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.title: Deployment Checklists
items.text: For deployment checklists, describe the trust boundary, input checks, failure handling and cleanup; keep credentials and real private data out of examples.

items.title: Maintenance and Version Updates
items.text: For maintenance and version updates, parse values to a date-time class first and verify formats, timezone assumptions and a boundary date.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Trace an input through one calculation to an output, then test missing, invalid and slow-operation behavior. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For building production-ready shiny apps, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

hints: Start with “Application Architecture” and identify the input and output before coding.
Use synthetic data and explicit validation; do not access production systems or expose credentials.
Test a boundary, missing, invalid or failure input relevant to this topic.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming external services always return valid data.
common_mistakes.why: Timeouts, authorization failures, rate limits and schema changes are normal failure cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Add timeouts, status/schema validation, least-privilege access and bounded retries.

common_mistakes.problem: Embedding credentials or sensitive rows in examples or logs.
common_mistakes.why: Secrets and private data can leak through source control or diagnostic output.
common_mistakes.fix: Use environment-based secret handling and synthetic examples; redact logs.

common_mistakes.problem: Leaving resources open after an error.
common_mistakes.why: Unclosed connections and files can leak resources or lock outputs.
common_mistakes.fix: Use reliable cleanup patterns and test both success and failure paths.
